reference.title: Barbell Clean and Jerk
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be read from this environment, gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the floor, hold through the clean; take a new breath in the rack, brace, hold through the dip, drive and catch; breathe out once the bar is locked out.
breathing.cadence: Pull about 0.8 s, clean 0.55 s, dip 0.3 s, drive and catch 0.35 s

prescription.frequency: 1-3 times a week, early in the session
prescription.tempo: Controlled first pull, explosive second pull and drive
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: technique-limited, every rep fast and crisp (NSCA guidance for power exercises).
prescription.progression: Add load in small steps once the catch positions are stable.

cues.text: Feet hip width under the bar, overhand grip just outside the shins, hips above the knees, back flat, shoulders over the bar.
Push the floor away; the bar slides up the shins to just above the knees with the back angle held.
Jump and shrug, pull under with the elbows fast round to the front, catch on the shoulders in a quarter squat.
Stand tall with the bar racked; reset the breath and the grip.
Short, straight dip: knees forward, trunk upright, heels down.
Drive up hard onto the toes, then punch under the bar and catch it on locked arms in a quarter squat.
Stand up with the bar over the back of the neck, arms locked.
Lower the bar to the shoulders, then to the thighs and back to the floor under control.

mistakes.fix: Arms long until the hips have finished the jump.
Dip straight down with the weight over the mid-foot and the trunk upright.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing the bar out instead of driving
mistakes.fix: Let the legs throw the bar; the arms punch you under it.
Lock the elbows hard and push up into the bar.

kinematics.setup: Plates on the floor; knees ≈78°, hip channel ≈138°, trunk ≈65° from vertical
kinematics.peak: Above the knees after the first pull: knees ≈19°, trunk ≈31°
kinematics.norm: Floor start like a deadlift; first pull to above the knees with the back angle held (NSCA power clean guide)

kinematics.setup: Second pull on the balls of the feet, bar to the lower chest with the elbows high
kinematics.peak: Quarter squat, knees ≈50°; bar on the front of the shoulders, elbows ≈26° from the trunk line
kinematics.norm: Power catch in a quarter squat with the bar on the front of the shoulders (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Dip: knees ≈22°, trunk upright, bar on the shoulders
kinematics.peak: Catch on locked arms (elbows ≈8°) in a quarter squat, knees ≈30°; standing: upper arm ≈165° from the trunk line, bar -1.5 cm from mid-foot
kinematics.norm: Dip about a quarter squat, drive onto the toes, catch on locked arms; the push press and jerk share the dip-drive pattern (Soriano 2024)

kinematics.setup: Overhand, 58 cm between the handle centres
kinematics.norm: Overhand, just outside the shoulders (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Set 0.8 s, first pull 0.8 s, clean 0.5 s
kinematics.peak: Dip 0.4 s, drive and catch 0.4 s, recover 0.8 s, down to the floor 3.6 s
kinematics.norm: Controlled first pull, explosive second pull and drive (clinical opinion)

cautions: Learn the lift with an empty bar under coaching; use bumper plates and a clear platform.
Know how to dump a missed jerk forward or backward.
Shoulder pain overhead or poor overhead mobility: stop at the clean.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: This animation shows a power jerk (feet stay planted); the split jerk catches with one foot forward and one back.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Drives the hip extension of the jump.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Drives the hip extension of the jump.
muscleNotes.quads_r: Extend the knees in the jump and catch the bar in the squat.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Extend the knees in the jump and catch the bar in the squat.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Hold the back angle in the pull and extend the hips.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Hold the back angle in the pull and extend the hips.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: The shrug at the top of the pull.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: The shrug at the top of the pull.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Rise onto the balls of the feet at full extension.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Rise onto the balls of the feet at full extension.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Lifts and turns the arms over to catch the bar.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Lifts and turns the arms over to catch the bar.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Elbows high and out in the pull under.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Elbows high and out in the pull under.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the back flat from the start to the catch.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the back flat from the start to the catch.
muscleNotes.core: Brace from set-up to the catch.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the bar (hook grip in practice).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the bar (hook grip in practice).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Keeps the arms long until the jump; works as the arms pull under.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Keeps the arms long until the jump; works as the arms pull under.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Turns the shoulder blades up to hold the bar overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Turns the shoulder blades up to hold the bar overhead.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Keep the bar close to the body in the pull.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Keep the bar close to the body in the pull.
